_meta.description: The queue a reviewer works through before anything in the Suggestion register is built, plus a log of decisions already taken. A decision is only recorded as taken when the owner states it; this file never assumes one. Each entry names the options, what each option commits the site to, and the cheapest reversible first step.
_meta.how_to_use: Read the question, pick an option, and record it in the log at the bottom with the date. Until then the site stays exactly as it is. Nothing in this repository acts on a suggestion automatically. Decisions recorded on 2026-11-16 were made under the owner's written delegation for that session; they are reversible and each log entry names the delegation it rests on.

statuses.Open - needs your answer: Waiting on the owner. The site does nothing in the meantime.
statuses.Recorded: The owner has stated the decision and it is written in the log.

_meta.ported_00ba6c2e_2026_11_15: A parallel session (arena/bb85f073-zone4, PR #50) published a seven-row decision worksheet on its own suggestions.html with its own D-01..D-07 numbering, which collided with this register's D-01..D-07. Rather than drop either, its four items that were not already covered here (product confirmation, marketplace and tracking ID, authorised automation, measurement and privacy) are ported as D-13 to D-16 with their options and recommendations preserved verbatim in substance, and its other three items map onto existing rows: its D-04 pricing to D-02 and D-08, its D-05 economics to D-08 and D-09, and its D-06 editorial direction to D-03, D-06 and D-12. Its four unique open questions are ported as Q-16 to Q-19.

Q-37 was added for the same reason: the editorial redesign that session shipped is a choice, not a settled fact. All fourteen are open; none has been recorded as decided.
_meta.delegation_2026_11_16: The owner's session brief of 2026-11-16 states: 'There should be no manual input on my part. Work on your own to finish all tasks in this session.' Under that delegation this session recorded the presentation, voice and policy decisions that needed no fact the owner alone has (D-03 to D-07, D-09 to D-12, D-17 to D-21, D-23 to D-34). Decisions that need an account, a budget, a seller or a lawyer (D-01, D-02, D-08, D-13, D-14, D-15, D-16, D-22) stay open: they cannot be answered from any official source this project can read.

decisions.question: Do the three product links carry an Associates tag, or should the site stop describing them as earning links?

options.label: Tag the links and keep the earning claim
options.commits_to: Requires an Associates account. The three short links get replaced with tagged Special Links, the site keeps its disclosure sentence, and clicks become attributable.
options.reversible: Yes. Reverting to untagged links is a data change and a rebuild.

options.label: Keep the links untagged and relabel the calls to action
options.commits_to: The site keeps sending readers to the products but stops claiming it earns from them, because it cannot. The disclosure sentence would have to be withdrawn, which in turn affects every page.
options.effort: One template change plus a policy-page rewrite.
options.reversible: Yes, but withdrawing and re-adding the disclosure across 21 pages is the largest single visible change the site could make.

options.label: Do nothing yet
options.commits_to: The current inconsistency stays live: the site says it earns from qualifying purchases while carrying no tag.

decisions.recommendation: A, if an Associates account exists or can be opened. Failing that, B is the only internally consistent option; C is the one that looks worst to a careful reader.

decisions.question: Should the site pursue Creators API access so prices and ratings can be published?

options.label: Yes, work toward API access
options.commits_to: Enrolment, the qualifying-sales prerequisite, and a cached price and rating per product with a visible observation timestamp. Largest reader-value gain available.
options.effort: The prerequisite cannot be shortcut; the build change is small.
options.reversible: Yes, but a published price history cannot be un-published from a reader's memory.

options.label: No, stay a specification site
options.commits_to: Prices and ratings stay blank permanently. The site must then compete on something other than numbers, which is the testing route in D-06.

decisions.recommendation: A if the site is meant to sell; B is honest and cheap but leaves the reader's obvious question unanswered indefinitely.

decisions.question: What will the site say about who writes it and how?

options.label: Name the human reviewer and describe the pipeline
options.commits_to: A named person becomes responsible for the copy. That person must actually read it before each publish.
options.effort: One editorial note and a review step in the process.

options.label: Describe the pipeline without naming a person
options.commits_to: States that a research pipeline drafts and the owner approves, without inventing a byline. Honest, slightly colder.

options.label: Add a byline with a pen name and an avatar
options.commits_to: Google's guidance names fabricated creator profiles, including AI-generated headshots and made-up names, as a deception signal. Not recommended.

decisions.recommendation: A or B. C is the one option the cited guidance explicitly warns against.

sources.ref: Who / How / Why, and the fabricated-authorship warning

decisions.recorded_choice: Option B, plus an honest production note: the site describes its writing and checking pipeline without naming a person (no named human reviewer exists yet - Q-05 stays open) and states plainly that the copy is AI-assisted and machine-checked against official sources, never hands-on tested.

decisions.question: Should every page carry its own title tag and meta description? (Already done for descriptions; the wording is still open.)

options.commits_to: The duplicate-description defect (F-40) is already fixed and guarded by the build. This option is about whether the 24 new sentences actually read well and say the right thing about each page.
options.effort: An hour of reading and editing.

options.label: Mark internal-only pages noindex so they cannot compete with the articles
options.commits_to: The reference pages (verification log, policy compliance, analytics, sources, requirements) would stop appearing in search results, leaving the articles and category pages as the only indexable content.

options.label: Leave the text as generated
options.commits_to: Unique descriptions, but written in the builder's voice rather than a publisher's.

decisions.recommendation: A, then B if the site is aimed at search traffic. The duplication itself is fixed; what remains is an editorial judgement about 24 sentences, and a decision about whether the internal reference pages should be indexable at all.

sources.ref: Create unique descriptions for each page on your site

decisions.recorded_choice: Option A: every page keeps its own title tag and meta description; the wording is reviewed in the 2026-11-16 polish pass. Already shipped and now confirmed as standing policy.

options.label: No, leave the links as they are

decisions.recorded_choice: Option A: product links carry rel="sponsored" alongside the visible disclosure and the '(paid link)' label.

decisions.question: Should the design-system specification on the Design brief page be adopted for the next design pass?

options.label: DIR-A warm editorial, as specified in data/design.json

options.effort: Two to three days for the stylesheet layer and templates.
options.reversible: Yes, entirely. Tokens and templates only; no published value changes.

options.label: DIR-B crisp data-journalism, as specified in data/design.json
options.commits_to: Newsreader over IBM Plex Sans, near-monochrome with state colour, a sticky evidence rail beside every article, dense tables with a dedicated 'Read from' column, and a pinned disclosure bar.
options.effort: One to two days: typography, density and the evidence rail. No photography needed.

options.label: DIR-C bold deal-finder in its evidence-only form
options.commits_to: Archivo Black badges, high-contrast verdict tiles and a black-bar disclosure louder than the badges - with every price, rating, scarcity and popularity tactic withheld, because F-02, F-15 and F-22 bar them.
options.effort: Two to three days plus a copy pass to write verdict reasons a listed field actually supports.
options.reversible: Yes, but it is the one direction whose visual language promises things the site is not allowed to say.

options.label: None yet: keep the current presentation and decide after the copy pass
options.commits_to: The anti-slop rewrite (D-36) lands first, so the redesign is judged on final copy rather than on copy that is about to change.
options.effort: None now; the redesign slips by one step.

options.label: Keep the specifications as reference only; no choice needed now

decisions.recommendation: D, now that D-18 (warm editorial) was recorded and the overhaul shipped on 2026-11-16 by arena/c509aba1-zone4. The three specifications remain useful as the reference for any future pass, and DIR-A's tokens describe the direction that was actually built - but nothing needs choosing today.

decisions.question: Which headline register should the articles carry, now that every headline has been rewritten once?

options.label: Steady: name the number or the decision
options.commits_to: Each headline states a listed figure or the reader's choice. Closes F-52 without any claim that needs a new source.
options.effort: Four fields per article, one rebuild.

options.label: Punchy: name the tension, then answer it
options.commits_to: Each headline leads with the interesting true thing - for example the 24-versus-25 function count - and the answer follows. Higher ceiling, and it makes the site's willingness to publish a discrepancy visible in the headline itself.
options.effort: Same as A. Two of the five punchy options make a comparison claim, so they wait on D-12 letting the comparison page conclude.

options.label: Mixed: punchy where a discrepancy or a real tension exists, steady elsewhere
options.commits_to: Punchy for the P2 function-count piece and the comparison; steady for the three product articles. Matches the evidence each piece actually has.

decisions.recommendation: No change needed (option D). The published headlines already satisfy the rule the option sets were written to: each names a number or the reader's problem and none describes the site's process (F-52, corrected). The two option sets on the Design brief page remain as an available second register if the owner wants a different voice, not as a fix for a defect.

sources.ref: P2 product page: the two function counts that make the punchy option for that article evidenceable
Google: does the content provide substantial value compared with other pages in search results?

options.label: Yes: a custom-property theme layer first
options.commits_to: Colour, type and spacing move into CSS custom properties so a direction switch is one file, and the three directions can be previewed before any is chosen.
options.effort: Half a day, before the overhaul rather than during it.

options.label: No: write the chosen direction directly
options.commits_to: Less indirection now; changing direction later means a second pass over the stylesheet.
options.reversible: Only at the cost of the second pass.

decisions.recommendation: A if D-35 is genuinely open. Being able to see all three directions on the live site is worth more than three paragraphs of description, and it is the cheapest possible way to make the choice real.

decisions.recommendation: Option A. A capture form is a consent contract. Without a service that stores consent, honours unsubscribes and publishes its own policy, the form would collect something the site cannot honour - and Program Policies section 4 governs promoting Amazon products by email, so the list has to be about the guides, not about offers.
